About Us
The Honest Company (NASDAQ: HNST) is a digitally-native consumer products company born in the Gen Z era to make purpose-driven consumer products designed for all people. Since its launch in 2012, Honest has been dedicated to creating thoughtfully formulated, safe and effective personal care, beauty, baby and household products, which are available via  honest.com , third-party ecommerce partners and approximately 50,000 retail locations across the United States, Canada and Europe. Based in Los Angeles, CA, the Company's mission, to inspire everyone to love living consciously, is driven by its values of transparency, trust, sustainability and a deep sense of purpose around what matters most to its consumers: their health, their families and their homes. For more information about the Honest Standard and the company, please visit  www.honest.com .
Our Mission
We're on a mission to empower people to live happy, healthy lives. We're a wellness brand with values rooted in consciousness, community, transparency, and design. Every day and in every way, we hold ourselves to an Honest standard. We believe that it is our responsibility to do our part to help create a healthy and sustainable future for all.
The Role
The Consumer Insights Data Analyst will serve as the objective source of truth on business and category performance. The ideal candidate is a curious, strategic thinker, detail oriented and a collaborative business partner who thrives in a fast-paced environment. This role owns data quality, builds the dashboards and visualizations the business runs on, and applies advanced analytics to explain performance and uncover growth opportunities, partnering cross-functionally to democratize data-driven decision making. This role is hybrid and open to either being located in Los Angeles, CA or Minneapolis, MN.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
The Data Analyst is responsible for duties including but not limited to the following:
Own the source of truth: Serve as the objective, single source of truth on business performance across syndicated data sources (e.g. Circana, Stackline) and retailer POS portals. Harmonize these sources into one consistent view of consumption, share, distribution, pricing, and promotion.
Ensure data quality and governance: Maintain data pipelines, product and retailer hierarchies, and common KPI definitions. Establish validation checks, cross-source reconciliation, and documentation to ensure data quality and accuracy.
Report on the state of the business: Deliver weekly, monthly, and quarterly performance reporting by brand, category, channel, and retailer. Proactively flag trends, risks, and opportunities, and explain the drivers behind the results.
Build dashboards and visualizations: Design, develop, and maintain intuitive, automated dashboards. Continuously improve usability, adoption, and refresh reliability.
Apply advanced analytics: Lead deep-dive analyses such as sales driver decomposition, price and promotion effectiveness, distribution and velocity, assortment and share of shelf, forecasting, and incrementality. Translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
Democratize data: Partner with cross-functional teams (e.g. Brand, Finance, Sales, etc.) to understand business questions and key success metrics. Train and enable stakeholders to find and use data independently, building data literacy and a culture of evidence-based decision making.
Tell the story: Synthesize data from multiple sources into concise narratives and presentations that influence strategy and unlock data-backed decision making.
Manage data partners: Serve as the primary point of contact for data vendors (e.g. Circana) managing deliverables, database builds, and issue resolution.
WHAT YOU’LL NEED
Experience: Minimum of 3–5 years in data analytics, sales or category analytics, or business intelligence within CPG or retail.
Education: Bachelor's degree in Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Business, or a related quantitative field required; an advanced degree is a plus.
Technical Skills:
Hands-on expertise with Circana, Stackline, NielsenIQ, or other retailer POS systems.
Strong command of CPG measures (e.g., consumption, distribution, velocity, base vs. incremental, dollar and unit share).
Advanced Excel and SQL; experience with Python or R for data manipulation and statistical modeling.
Proficiency building dashboards in Power BI, Hex, Tableau, or similar BI tools.
Experience with statistical methods such as regression, forecasting, and price elasticity modeling.
Working knowledge of data modeling, ETL, and cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks) is preferred.
Key Competencies:
Relentless attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy and integrity.
Ability to reconcile and synthesize disparate data sources into a single, trusted view.
Strong business acumen and the ability to translate complex analyses into clear, actionable recommendations.
Collaborative partner who can influence and educate stakeholders at all levels.
Adept at managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
Additional Skills:
Excellent written, verbal, and data storytelling skills.
Proactive and curious, with a drive to automate and continuously improve processes.
Experience managing data vendor relationships.
Passion for enabling others through data literacy and self-service tools.
Compensation
The pay range for this role is $61,000 – $76,000. Actual compensation is based on many factors including but not limited to depth of experience, skill level, ability, knowledge, education, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.
The total rewards package for this position may also include base, annual incentive plan, benefits, retirement plan, equity, and Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

About the job
Turn your machine learning coursework into insight that helps AI infrastructure run more reliably.
As a Machine Learning and Data Science Engineer Intern, you will analyze telemetry from data center facilities and engineering infrastructure. You will apply data science and machine learning methods to real operational data.
Your work will help engineers spot patterns, understand anomalies and make better-informed decisions. You will learn how infrastructure data connects to reliability, performance and day-to-day operations.
You will clean and explore datasets, build reproducible analyses and evaluate predictive models. You will also create visualizations, document assumptions and share findings with technical colleagues.
This internship gives you practical experience with real-world infrastructure data, supported by engineers who value curiosity and clear thinking.
The team and culture
You will work with the Facilities Reliability Engineering team in Austin. The team supports infrastructure used to develop and test the next generation of AI systems.
Work happens through clear operational questions, shared data exploration, prototype analysis and practical review with engineers. Decisions are shaped by evidence, operational knowledge, reproducible results and honest discussion of uncertainty.
You will own defined tasks with guidance, feedback and room to ask questions. As an intern, you will build confidence by turning data into insight engineers can use.
What we’re looking for
Current enrollment at junior or senior undergraduate level, or in a master's program, in data science, AI, machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field
Foundational knowledge of machine learning, statistics and data analysis through coursework, research, projects or practical experience
Programming experience in Python, with familiarity using common data-analysis libraries
Experience preparing, exploring, analyzing and visualizing datasets
Understanding of supervised machine learning concepts, including regression, classification, model training and model evaluation
Clear communication, a methodical approach to problem-solving and willingness to seek guidance when needed
While we have outlined a set of requirements, we value transferable skills and diverse experiences.
Benefits
Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
Comprehensive healthcare: Medical, dental and vision coverage to help keep you and your family healthy
Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
Tax-advantaged healthcare savings: Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) and Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) to help you make the most of your healthcare spending
Peace of mind protection: Disability and life insurance to provide financial security when you need it most
Retirement planning support: A 401(k) plan to help you invest in your future
Commuter benefits: Help cover the cost of your daily commute
Wellbeing resources: Access to wellness services that support your physical and mental health
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Confidential advice and support for you and your family across a range of personal, financial and wellbeing matters
We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.
We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognize that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, just let us know - we're happy to support you.
